title: Majority Element (n/3 times)
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Find all elements appearing more than n/3 times (at most two can exist).
intuition: At most k-1 = 2 elements can exceed n/3, so keep two candidates and two counters. Cancelling a triple of distinct values cannot eliminate a true majority.

approaches.title: Better: hash counts
approaches.code:
from collections import Counter


def majority3_hash(a: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    return [k for k, v in Counter(a).items() if v > n // 3]

approaches.title: Optimal: two candidates, two counters
approaches.idea: Then verify both with a second pass.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[1,1,1,3,3,2,2,2]
candidates settle on 1 and 2
verify: count(1)=3 > 2, count(2)=3 > 2 -> [1,2]
approaches.whyWorks: Each decrement removes three distinct occurrences, so an element with > n/3 copies survives.

edgeCases: Exactly n/3 (not strictly greater) must be rejected
commonMistakes: Checking candidate equality after the count == 0 branches, which mis-assigns duplicates
followUps: Why can at most k-1 such elements exist?
interviewInsight: The branch ordering is the bug factory here — write the equality checks first, deliberately.
